API Reference¶

app¶

Flask Web Application — Module 3, JHU Software Concepts¶

Connects to PostgreSQL, runs 10 analytical queries on the applicants table, displays results in a styled web page, and provides:

  • “Pull Data” button → runs scrape.py to fetch NEW GradCafe data (appends only)

  • “Update Analysis” button → refreshes displayed query results

Thread-safe: uses a threading.Lock to prevent simultaneous scrape requests.

app.create_app(test_config=None)[source]¶

Flask application factory.

Usage (production):

app = create_app()

Usage (testing):

app = create_app({"TESTING": True, "DATABASE_URL": None})
Parameters:

test_config (dict or None) –

If provided, these values override the default configuration. Common keys:

  • TESTING (bool) — enable Flask testing mode

  • DATABASE_URL (str|None) — PostgreSQL connection string. None means “skip the database” (used when tests mock it).

scrape¶

GradCafe Applicant Data Scraper Extracts program name, university, status, date added, result URL, comments, semester, international status, GRE scores, GPA, and more from The GradCafe survey/search results using Selenium and BeautifulSoup. Handles pagination and saves results as JSON.

Site structure (modern Tailwind-based redesign): - Search URL: https://www.thegradcafe.com/survey?q=<query>&sort=newest - Results in a <table> with rows:

  • Data row (<tr> with 5 <td>): School, Program (with degree), Added On, Status badge, Actions column (result URL link)

  • Detail row 1 (<tr class=”tw-border-none”>, colspan=100%): status (mobile), semester term, international status, GPA, GRE scores

  • Detail row 2 (optional, <tr class=”tw-border-none”>): applicant comments

  • Pagination via “Next” links at bottom

scrape.extract_page_results(driver)[source]¶

Extract all result entries from the current page using BeautifulSoup. The table alternates between:

  • Data row (5 <td> cells)

  • Detail row 1 (colspan=100%, status badges + term + GPA + GRE)

  • Detail row 2 (optional, colspan=100%, comments in <p>)

Returns a list of record dicts.

scrape.get_next_page_url(driver)[source]¶

Find the ‘Next’ page link on the current page.

scrape.parse_comments(comment_cell)[source]¶

Parse the optional second detail row that contains applicant comments. The comment text is in a <p> tag.

scrape.parse_data_row(row)[source]¶

Parse a data <tr> that has 5 <td> cells. Returns a dict with university, program, degree, added_on, status, result_url.

scrape.parse_detail_badges(detail_cell)[source]¶

Parse the detail row badges. Badges are <div> elements with rounded-md styling. They contain one of:

  • Status badge: “Wait listed on May 29” (mobile only, hidden on md+)

  • Term badge: “Fall 2026”, “Spring 2027”

  • International badge: “International” or “American”

  • GPA badge: “GPA 3.50”, “GPA 3.85”

  • GRE badge: “GRE 168”, “GRE V 160”, “GRE AW 4.00”

  • Other misc badge

Returns a dict with parsed fields.

scrape.parse_status_badge_desktop(cell)[source]¶

Parse the desktop status column (column 3). Contains a badge div with text like:

“Wait listed on May 29” “Rejected on May 22” “Accepted on Apr 30”

scrape.scrape_gradcafe(search_query='computer science', max_pages=1500, output_file='applicant_data.json', headless=True)[source]¶

Main scraping function for The GradCafe.

Parameters:

  • search_query – Search term for GradCafe.

  • max_pages – Maximum number of pages to scrape (0 = unlimited).

  • output_file – Path to the output JSON file.

  • headless – Whether to run browser in headless mode.

Returns:

List of all scraped records.

scrape.setup_driver(headless=True)[source]¶

Configure and return a Chrome WebDriver.
